root_cause.text: The flow dissector attempted to handle PPPoE Protocol Field Compression (PFC) frames by conditionally adjusting the network header offset, which resulted in a 1-byte payload shift and 4-byte misalignment, causing unaligned memory access exceptions on architectures like MIPS.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "having a compressed (1-byte) protocol field means the subsequent PPP payload is shifted by one byte, causing 4-byte misalignment for the network header and an unaligned access exception on some architectures." The patch removes the PFC handling code (the if-else that conditionally subtracts 1 from PPPOE_SES_HLEN) and always uses the uncompressed offset, forcing compressed frames to be rejected because the resulting protocol field fails ppp_proto_is_valid(). The stack trace confirms the crash in __skb_flow_dissect due to an unaligned access (ExcCode 04).

intent_record.intent_summary: Drop support for PPPoE frames with compressed protocol field (PFC) to simplify code and reject non-standard frames.
intent_record.what: Removed conditional handling of compressed PPP protocol fields (PFC). Previously, if the protocol field had the LSB of the most significant octet set (0x0100), the code would shift the protocol byte and adjust nhoff by PPPOE_SES_HLEN - 1; now it always adds PPPOE_SES_HLEN. Updated comment to explain that PFC frames are not processed and will be rejected.
intent_record.how: PPPoE frames using compressed protocol field will no longer be correctly parsed; they will be treated as invalid by ppp_proto_is_valid(), resulting in FLOW_DISSECT_RET_OUT_BAD.

grouping_result.intent: Drop support for PPPoE frames with compressed protocol field (PFC) to simplify code and reject non-standard frames.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by dropping support for PPPoE PFC frames, thereby removing the problematic offset adjustment that led to unaligned memory access.

This statement directly causes a 1-byte payload shift in the network header offset when PFC is active, resulting in 4-byte misalignment and unaligned memory access exceptions.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the PPPoE case (lines ~82-98), the code reads a struct containing pppoe_hdr and proto, and then adds PPPOE_SES_HLEN. This assumes the PPP protocol field is always present, but when Protocol Field Compression (PFC) is used, the proto field is omitted. This causes a 2-byte offset error and subsequent unaligned memory access when parsing IP headers.
